elaine (support): quick heads-up — multiple customers (EU region) opened tickets about sudden p95/p99 spikes and intermittent 504s on the hosted text-gen endpoint after yesterday's infra push. some report timeouts + auth retries. 

jordan (oncall-sre): ack, looking. any customer IDs or short repro?

elaine (support): CS forwarded logs from acme-marketing and freya-payments. pattern: small-batch (<4 tokens) realtime flows see p95 jump from ~120ms to ~420ms, p99 >1.1s. errors during bursty KV-cache warmups.

oliver (cs): acme sample traces: `POST /v1/generate` end->end increased, token-level latency per-step shows host stall.

jordan (oncall-sre): initial metrics: host-level NVMe queue depth and avg svctm spiked on several eu-west nodes. suspect storage IO contention. did we roll any driver/kernel/CUDA changes yesterday?

liam (eng-infra): we pushed a node image to eu-west pool at ~02:10 UTC: kernel 6.1.12 -> 6.1.14 and nvidia driver 535.x -> 536.2 (CUDA runtime unchanged). also bumped NVMe queue scheduler defaults (qsize backpressure tweak).

maya (eng-ml): we also rolled a model-serving runtime patch to improve KV-cache persistence. could interact with IO pattern.

jordan (oncall-sre): ok, reproduction plan: 1) run small-batch, high-concurrency replay against a repro node 2) capture `iostat -x`, `nvme top`, `dmesg` 3) capture per-request kernel wait stacks.

liam (eng-infra): running quick repro now on canary host. snippet of what I'm seeing on canary: 
```
$ iostat -x 1 5
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  rrqm/s  wrqm/s r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1         150.00  300.00  8192.00 16384.00 0.00   0.00   1.20   6.40   0.45   95.00
```

liam (eng-infra): `%util` climbs to >90 during burst; kernel backlog visible. dmesg shows `blk_mq: scheduling latency` warnings on some hosts.

maya (eng-ml): that matches what we saw in token-level latencies — the runtime stalls on occasional NVMe waits while loading KV shards.

jordan (oncall-sre): immediate mitigation options: 
- divert realtime small-batch traffic to eu fallback pool (older image)
- temporary increase NVMe queue-depth at driver level / tune elevator back to noop for test
- throttle/pre-warm KV-cache outside latency-critical path
- rollback driver on canary to 535.x if rollback quick

elaine (support): customers want ETA and mitigation now. recommend routing fallback while you triage.

liam (eng-infra): applying routing rule now: tag `small-batch-realtime` -> eu-fallback-pool (older image, no 536 driver). monitoring.

ops-bot: routing rule applied by liam at 9423456788.

jordan (oncall-sre): starting a canary rollback of driver on 2 repro nodes to 535.95, will re-run replay.

liam (eng-infra): also tried switching scheduler to `noop` on repro host: `echo noop > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler` — p95 dropped ~60ms in quick test.

maya (eng-ml): long-term we need to avoid KV-cache hot loads touching NVMe on the hot path. options: pre-warm into memcache, increase in-memory caching, or move KV shards to higher IOPS devices.

jordan (oncall-sre): repro after rollback: p95 on canary returned to baseline ~130ms, nvme `%util` down to ~45%. driver rollback looks promising.

oliver (cs): passing rollback and routing updates to customers — they'll confirm when traffic hits fallback. :thumbsup:

liam (eng-infra): next actions: 
- roll back driver in eu-west staging and hold release (liam, 1h)
- run full fleet quick probe to find other impacted pools (jordan, 2h)
- add ephemeral IOPS cgroup limit for noisy jobs as emergency safety (liam, 3h)
- performance postmortem and fix for KV-cache path (maya + eng-ml, next-day)

jordan (oncall-sre): also creating short-term mitigation: add route-level automatic fallback policy to route small-batch requests to pre-warmed nodes if observed host `disk_util > 80%`.

elaine (support): thanks — I'll update CS queue with the mitigation plan and ETA.

maya (eng-ml): note: if we keep rollback, we should test the runtime KV-cache patch against 535 driver before re-rolling 536. scheduling a matrix test.

ops-bot: incident tagged `p95-hostio-eu-smallbatch` and priority `P1` at 9423456790.

jordan (oncall-sre): closing loop: rollback + routing fallback reduced customer-reported errors to zero for active test tickets. keeping this open for 24h monitoring and will produce a short postmortem doc with timeline + root cause theories.

elaine (support): great, pushing closure notes to customers and will reopen if they see anything else. :white_check_mark:
